design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. Gabriel Navarro asks only to finish the cancellation of his Kessler Shield contract (KS-4426107, Exclusionary, sold 2024-04-12 at Kessler Honda Beavercreek on used-vehicle deal KHB-24-40517 for his 2020 Honda Pilot) after trading the Pilot in, and to learn the refund. The traded-vehicle refund rule states two waits: it 'is not computed until the contract's latest component repair line denied for lack of maintenance (by decision date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history) has been re-decided and whatever that re-decision owes the holder has been paid, wherever that line is on an engine, transmission or drive axle whose coverage switch is true, the latest visit redeemed on the Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal is not reinstated and is dated on or before that line's repair-order diagnosis and fewer than the coverage level's maintenance look-back months before it (the difference between the two dates' calendar months, less one where the diagnosis date's day of the month is earlier than the visit's), the waiting period is over or waived (the contract was sold on its vehicle's purchase deal under a coverage level that waives it for such a contract, or the diagnosis date is more than the waiting-period days after the sale date and the line's odometer is at least the waiting miles beyond the odometer at sale), the repair order's diagnosis date and the line's odometer fall within the term, and that repair order carries a diagnostic fee on exactly one concern line together with the store's customer-pay labor on that concern line, not wholly credited back as a comeback repair, closed on or after the day the line was decided' and it 'is fixed only after the contract's latest component repair line denied as not covered (by decision date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history) has been re-decided and whatever that re-decision owes the holder has been paid, wherever that line is on a component group that is not an internally lubricated one (engine, transmission or drive axle) and whose coverage switch is true, the waiting period is over or waived (the contract was sold on its vehicle's purchase deal under a coverage level that waives it for such a contract, or the diagnosis date is more than the waiting-period days after the sale date and the line's odometer is at least the waiting miles beyond the odometer at sale), the repair order's diagnosis date and the line's odometer fall within the term, and that repair order carries a diagnostic fee on exactly one concern line together with the store's customer-pay labor on that concern line, not wholly credited back as a comeback repair, closed on or after the day the line was decided'. The ledger holds exactly those two wrong denials (cooling line of CLM-4439217 as not covered on an Exclusionary that covers cooling; engine line of CLM-4452086 for lack of maintenance with Kessler Care visit 5 two months before the diagnosis), both paid by the holder on customer pay. The agent must discover both, price each repayment from the store's customer-pay rows (5 and 6 factors), then price the refund (5 factors) from two purchase deals, the repair orders and the request. Each problem has exactly one target tool.

SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 6, 5] -> C1 coverage re-decision 5, B1 maintenance re-decision 6, R1 traded-vehicle refund 5. Task 1 claims vsc_ext_coverage_denial_reimbursement (reimburse_coverage_denial_repair_73971dca, agent), vsc_ext_maintenance_denial_reimbursement (reimburse_maintenance_denial_repair_6315e699, agent), vsc_ext_traded_vehicle_refund (accept_traded_vehicle_cancellation_f71aca80, user). Task 0 holds the waiting-period re-decision, the rental line and the kept-vehicle refund; scopes are disjoint by denial reason (waiting_period / lack_of_maintenance / component_not_covered), by benefit (rental) and by cancel reason (customer_request / vehicle_sold_or_traded). None of task 0's state_due scopes is lit here (no waiting-period denial, no loaner on either RO).

PROBLEM TREE. Root R1 (user). R1 -> B1 value_input on redecided_count (action form, negated 'is not computed until' — a refund hold as the desk states it); R1 -> C1 state_gate on vsc_ledger.claim_line_type (action form, affirmative 'is fixed only after'). Each sentence names the completed re-decision of the contract's latest denial of its reason within that re-decision's scope (stated in the sentence as record tests), with whatever it owes paid (fallback reason: a re-decision that owes nothing books no line, so no record state tells a decided line from an undecided one), and no tool, id or code token; exactly one write of this difficulty completes each re-decision (the maintenance re-decision tool books paid lines on lack-of-maintenance claims, the coverage re-decision tool on not-covered claims). False at the opening: both denied lines exist with no paid line; claims_paid_total 0.00. Order: C1 and B1 are parallel and commute (different claims and ROs; limit far from binding; both orders run: 1080.91 / 6783.37 / 2035.27); gold books C1 (older claim) then B1, then R1. Deletion sensitivity: skip B1 -> refund 2010.27 (fee 25.00) and missing row; skip C1 -> missing 1080.91 row, claims_paid_total 6783.37 vs 7864.28.

FACTOR CARD. C1 (expected 1080.91; all-baseline 1193.10): cover_labor_rule method T1 charged 506.54 < list 533.20 (baseline standard 533.20 -> 1107.57); cover_parts_rule parameter T2 list 487.90 less goodwill 45.00 (-> 1125.91); cover_diag_share parameter T1 half credited -> 86.00 (-> 1166.91); cover_supplies_share method T1 whole 40.52 (-> 1040.39); cover_waste_share method T1 cooling whole 4.95 (-> 1075.96). B1 (expected 6783.37; all-baseline 6858.40): lube_labor_rule method T1 2333.92 < 2373.60 (-> 6823.05); lube_parts_rule parameter T2 4412.80 less goodwill 100.00 (-> 6883.37); lube_diag_share parameter T1 86.00 (-> 6869.37); lube_visit_deductible method T1 selling store KHB + disappearing deductible -> none (-> 6683.37; multi-source); lube_supplies_share method T2 49.95 x 2333.92/2530.00 = 46.08 (-> 6737.29; near-miss: whole fee); lube_waste_share method T2 4.95 x 2333.92/2530.00 = 4.57 (-> 6778.80). R1 (expected 2035.27; all-baseline 1932.19): trade_measure_day method T1 Kessler Care sold-or-traded cancellation 2026-09-28 (-> 1990.94; multi-source plan ledger, sale date, request date; cross-difficulty maintenance); trade_reading parameter T1 cancellation odometer 73684 (-> 2036.88; near-miss RO 71700 below certified 73520); trade_miles_start parameter T1 delivery odometer 36893 (-> 2032.98); trade_credit_days parameter T1 4 days (-> 2028.13); trade_fee_rule parameter T1 0.00 after the engine repayment (-> 1985.27; tier 2 Silver loyalty fee 25.00 without it; cross-difficulty service). The lesser-of shape is tuned so time share 0.509858 and mileage share 0.509453 sit 0.0004 apart: each time-side and mileage-side factor moves the result alone. R1 carries no elapsed-rounding factor because the elapsed days run to the measuring day (a factor output) and a rounding factor on them would read another factor (XF A.1).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Claim writes: active_contract_for_claim (status active); within_term (RO dates 2025-11-03 and 2026-08-17 <= 2029-04-12, odometers <= 111850; inclusive); waiting_period_over (waived: sold on a deal; both repairs long after 30 days / 1000 miles anyway); maintenance proof (engine: visit 2026-05-27 in the look-back; cooling not lubricated); factory coverage (basic expired 2022-10-25, powertrain 2024-10-25, used warranty 2024-05-16; emissions reaches neither); limit 40000.00. Deductible: base rule (selling store, disappearing) stated in the coverage re-decision's standard repayment; overwritten with a declared ladder for the maintenance re-decision. Cancellation: active_to_cancel and signed_request (vehicle_sold_or_traded, 2026-10-19, 73520, submitted). Free look: 920 days after sale with claims paid -> no flat refund; original deal closed, not unwound.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Coverage repayment: CLM-4439217 / RO 446908 / cooling / 60020; rows of RO 446908 line A and its RO-level fees. Maintenance repayment: CLM-4452086 / RO 447652 / engine / 71700; line A rows; line B (brake pads) rows excluded except as the 'other concern line' in the fee proportions. Refund: request on file; deal KHB-24-40517 (start odometer, credited days); the Kessler Care plan's sold-or-traded cancellation (measuring day 2026-09-28, reading 73684); latest RO odometer (71700, near-miss); service account (fee tier 2).

WORLD ROWS. Customer, store KHB, Pilot and Passport, both deals with their money histories (KHB-24-40517: 31450.00 + doc 299.00 + e-filing 24.00 + title/registration 99.50 + Ohio 6.75 percent tax 2122.88; 1000.00 deposit applied at delivery, 3852.75 down, Fifth Third funding 29142.63 = 33659.18 less 3995.00 VSC and 521.55 plan; KHB-26-41862: 44980.00 + 299.00 + 24.00 + 99.50 + tax 6.75 percent x (44980.00 - 23600.00 trade) = 1443.15 + negative equity 18.42; 1000.00 deposit, 9451.49 down, American Honda funding 36412.58; both closed at 0.00), contract, two denied lines, request, Silver service account, 20 RO rows (two ROs) and 3 repair authorizations (diagnostic-credit window, estimates = billed), Kessler Care plan with load + 5 visits (maintenance proof; plan-paid visits leave no service rows) and its 2026-09-28 sold-or-traded cancellation (request, cancelled visit, 85.95 refund calculation and its 2026-10-06 payment to Fifth Third Bank; measuring day and reading), 4 warranty coverages. Automatic clauses: contract term to 2029, plan cancelled 2026-09-28 with its 85.95 refund paid to the lienholder 2026-10-06, deals closed, service balance 0.00 — nothing else falls due. Residue: earlier service history is not read and not seeded; the points balance 5949 is the two seeded RO awards (older points expired).

PERSONA. Chatty teacher; volunteers only the traded-in Pilot, the signed cancellation and the refund question; identity on request (name, phone, licence last four, email alternative); odometer 73520 from memory on request; defers repair history to the records; passive consent to settle what the contract owes; runs the user tool with the values given; closes on confirmation.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate + verify -> contract -> ledger (two wrong denials) -> request -> deals -> each deal's money history -> vehicles -> warranties -> service account -> RO lines -> authorizations -> store -> plan + visits + plan cancellation -> coverage repayment 1080.91 (step 18) -> maintenance repayment 6783.37 (step 20) -> hand over the cancellation: 2026-10-19, 73520, pro_rata, 2035.27 (step 22).

VERIFICATION. Scratch run (evalc.full/sens over check_compute.build_env): C1 1080.91 and B1 6783.37 on the opening world (each order), R1 2035.27 after both; per-factor and all-baseline figures as above; skip-B1 refund 2010.27. Gates: worklog.md.

DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. The published refund rule shows two waits; the ledger shows a cooling denial on a level that covers cooling and an engine maintenance denial with a Kessler Care visit two months earlier -> repay both; then the refund from the trade deal, the original deal, the repair orders and the request. Same objects, order and figures as gold.

ROUNDS 2-3 (audit revisions 1-2). Charter changes re-run on this world with gold unchanged (1080.91 / 6783.37 / 2035.27; every factor_sensitivity and baseline_result figure identical). Both re-decision scopes state their record tests and this world meets them (coverage: latest component_not_covered line CLM-4439217, cooling, sold on the deal, within the term, one diagnosed concern line, line-A labor not wholly comeback-credited and closed 2025-11-05 after the 2025-11-04 decision; maintenance: latest lack_of_maintenance line CLM-4452086, engine, latest visit 2026-05-27 on the plan sold on the contract's deal, not reinstated, two months before the 2026-08-17 diagnosis, line-A labor closed 2026-08-26 after the 2026-08-18 decision). The maintenance deductible ladder follows the base rule (tier 1 here). Supplies and waste shares are labelled method; money rounds half up to the cent (compute adds 0.000000001 before RND; every RND argument on this world, including all factor and baseline substitutions, sits at least 0.000104 from a half cent). The refund's waits are stated in the action form (rounds 5-6; each wait restates its resolver's scope as plain record tests, so an out-of-scope latest denial, or a claim without a charged Kessler loaner at a level with a rental benefit, is plainly outside it): the refund waits until each latest denial has been re-decided with whatever it owes paid, so every positive repayment stays inside the wait and a re-decision owing nothing needs no line; here the deductible taken is 0.00 (selling store KHB, disappearing deductible) and the limit is far off, so each wait is unmet at the opening and clears once its resolver writes. Round 3 world change: the Kessler Care plan KC-4431560 was cancelled on 2026-09-28 for the vehicle being sold or traded (request, cancelled visit, refund calculation), and the refund's measuring day and first reading tier now read that cancellation (tied to the covered vehicle through the plan sold on the contract's deal) instead of the new-vehicle deal, whose trade-in appraisal no record ties to the Pilot; the second measuring-day tier is a loan payoff recorded on the GAP waiver sold on the contract's deal (none here). The reading's repair-order tier states its same-day tie rule. All 19 overwrites name their own case and siblings and restate base for every other case; the rental overwrite covers every rental it does not price.

ROUND 9 (renderer scan render_r1, F1-F5). Rule == compute at every edge: the rental start day's tier 2 now also tests that the loaner went out on the diagnosis day; the refund fee tiers read the contract's latest denied component-repair line and test that a paid component-repair line on the same claim number, repair order and component group was entered later; every re-decision's 'already repaid' check keys on the claim number, repair order and component group; plan and GAP lookups on the contract's deal are skipped for a contract sold on its own (empty deal id); the starting-odometer tiers apply only to terms counted from the sale date, so in-service-date terms keep the term start odometer. Labor and parts tiers no longer name a discount program the compute does not test. This world sits on the same tiers; gold, order and every figure are unchanged.

ROUND 10 (audit revision_9, RED-R9a / RED-R9b). The refund fee tiers state their same-day convention: a paid component-repair line entered on or after the day of the latest denial (same claim, repair order and group) counts as later paid, and the compute tests repaid_day >= denied_day. The rental start day's second tier names which denial: the claim's latest denial by decision date (the compute's LATEST). This world is unaffected (denial and repayment on different days; one denied line per claim); gold, order and every figure are unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Gabriel Navarro, a high-school chemistry teacher in Kettering, Ohio — friendly, a little chatty, and careful to get things right, though you don't remember paperwork details well. Late last month you traded your 2020 Honda Pilot in at Kessler Honda Beavercreek and drove home a new Passport. You had bought a Kessler Shield service contract on the Pilot back when you bought it there in 2024, and on Monday you stopped by the store and signed the form to cancel that contract since the car is gone. Nobody has told you what you'll get back, so you're calling the Kessler support desk.

You start by saying: "Hi there — I traded in my Pilot a few weeks ago and signed the papers to cancel the service contract that was on it. I'm hoping you can finish that cancellation and tell me what refund I'm getting." If the agent asks why you are cancelling, you say: "The Pilot's gone — I traded it in on the Passport." You don't have anything else you want to take care of on this call.

When asked who you are, you give your name, Gabriel Navarro, and your phone number, 9375554629. If they need another detail, you give the last four of your driver's license, 4931; if they ask for an email instead, it's gabriel.navarro@gmail.com. You don't know the contract number offhand and ask them to look it up under your name. If they ask what mileage you wrote on the cancellation form, you say you put down 73520, which was your best guess from memory. If they ask about past repairs or about the car's history, you say the store's records will be more accurate than your memory and they should go by those.

You don't know how refunds are figured and you have no number in mind. If the agent explains that something on the contract has to be settled or paid out to you before the cancellation can go through, you say that's fine and to go ahead and take care of it; if they tell you it's done, you say "Oh, great, thank you" and let them continue.

When the agent tells you the refund amount and hands the cancellation over for you to accept, you run it yourself, entering exactly the details the agent gives you (the contract, your request, the effective date, the odometer, the refund basis and the amount). Once it confirms the contract is cancelled and the refund is recorded as due, you thank the agent warmly and say goodbye. If the agent only quotes a figure without handing anything over, you say "That sounds fine — please go ahead and finish it," and wait for them to hand it to you.

edges.condition: For the contract's latest vsc_claim_denied component_repair line with denial_reason lack_of_maintenance (first listed on a same-day tie), where its group is engine/transmission/drive_axle with its covers_ switch true, the latest non-reinstated maintenance_visit_redeemed entry of the plan sold on the contract's deal is dated on or before the RO diagnosis date with MONTHS(visit, diagnosis) < maintenance_proof_lookback_months, the waiting period is over or waived, the RO is within the term and carries exactly one service_diagnostic_fee_charged row and customer-pay labor on that line, net of comeback credit above zero, closed on or after the denial's entry_date: the re-decision is made, leaving a vsc_claim_paid component_repair line under its claim number where it owes a positive amount and no line where it owes nothing. A latest lack_of_maintenance denial outside those tests is outside the wait.
edges.policy_source: The refund on a traded-vehicle cancellation is not computed until the contract's latest component repair line denied for lack of maintenance (by decision date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history) has been re-decided and whatever that re-decision owes the holder has been paid, wherever that line is on an engine, transmission or drive axle whose coverage switch is true, the latest visit redeemed on the Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal (a contract sold on its own has no such plan) is not reinstated and is dated on or before that line's repair-order diagnosis and fewer than the coverage level's maintenance look-back months before it (the difference between the two dates' calendar months, less one where the diagnosis date's day of the month is earlier than the visit's), the waiting period is over or waived (the contract was sold on its vehicle's purchase deal under a coverage level that waives it for such a contract, or the diagnosis date is more than the waiting-period days after the sale date and the line's odometer is at least the waiting miles beyond the odometer at sale), the repair order's diagnosis date and the line's odometer fall within the term, and that repair order carries a diagnostic fee on exactly one concern line together with the store's customer-pay labor on that concern line, not wholly credited back as a comeback repair, closed on or after the day the line was decided.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two repayments are parallel prerequisites of the refund and commute: they sit on different claims and repair orders, read nothing the other writes except the claims-paid total, and the aggregate limit (40000.00) is far from binding. Run both ways: coverage first -> 1080.91 then 6783.37; maintenance first -> 6783.37 then 1080.91; the refund is 2035.27 either way and the terminal rows are identical.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the maintenance repayment leaves redecided_count 0: the fee becomes the trade loyalty fee 25.00 and refund_amount moves 2035.27 -> 2010.27; the engine paid row is also missing.
Skipping the coverage repayment leaves the 1080.91 cooling paid row out of the terminal ledger and claims_paid_total at 6783.37 instead of 7864.28 (the refund figure is unchanged).
